Bug_Details:
Using a collection function with itself as the argument. Invoking a collection method with the same collection as the argument is likely
incorrect. collection.addAll(collection) may cause an infinite loop, duplicate the
elements, or do nothing, depending on the type of Collection and
implementation class.
collection.retainAll(collection) is a no-op.
collection.removeAll(collection) is the same as collection.clear().
collection.containsAll(collection) is always true.
Bug_Explanation: In Java, if we call addAll() with the same list as the argument, it will duplicate the elements in the list. This can lead to an infinite loop, duplicate the elements, or do nothing, depending on the type of Collection and implementation class.
Trigger_Explanation: This test case triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method in the `CollectionBug` class. The `showBug` method tries to add all elements of its list to itself, which is not allowed because `ArrayList` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when this happens.
